questions.key_step: Even r gives rational terms; five computed terms
questions.justification: Single familiar move (even r), five short evaluations; no insight needed.

questions.key_step: Express three coefficients as multiples of nCr; two linear equations
questions.justification: Routine rewriting of three coefficients and two linear equations; Level 1-2 on this scale, rated 1 because each step is one standard formula.

questions.key_step: Recognise z=-i*omega; cancellation then a power
questions.justification: Needs the polar/omega form of z and three routine simplifications; chain of standard steps with a clean cancellation.

questions.key_step: Write 7^103 as (345-2)^34 type expansions twice (or Euler criterion)
questions.justification: Standard binomial remainder trick applied twice (343 = 345-2, 256 = 253+3); routine but multi-step with arithmetic risk.

questions.key_step: Four statements, each a counting check; B and C disjoint by parity
questions.justification: Four statements to verify with small counting; each is routine but all must be checked.

questions.key_step: Last digit 2 or 7 then casework on position of 7 with leading-digit restriction
questions.justification: Casework with the leading-digit restriction and a last-digit condition; one slip changes the answer, though options help.
One standard identity r*C(9,r)=9*C(8,r-1) plus two binomial sums; routine chain, option-based.

questions.key_step: Only two equilateral triangles
questions.justification: Single observation (only alternate vertices); one-move question.

questions.key_step: Count run sequences of lengths 3,4,5 carefully; expectation
questions.justification: Careful listing of runs of exactly 3,4,5 heads and a complement; moderate precision risk but small numbers.

questions.key_step: Shift origin; variance of -d,0,d
questions.justification: Shift-invariance of variance then one equation; one familiar move.

questions.key_step: Identical + distinct selection; half of 2^21
questions.justification: Identical-plus-distinct selection reduces to half of 2^21; one idea, little arithmetic.

questions.key_step: Four outcomes of the stopping rule; all-loss branch is the trap
questions.justification: Needs all four outcomes of the stopping rule; the all-loss case is easy to miss, otherwise routine.

questions.key_step: Two divisibility conditions (12|r and 3|n) then least n
questions.justification: Two divisibility conditions and a least-value argument; the second condition (3|n) is easy to overlook.

questions.key_step: P(w_n)=2^-n and spotting that 6 is not 2k+3l with k,l>=1
questions.justification: Two linked ideas: normalising a halving law and identifying the set 2k+3l (positive k,l) with the missing value 6.

questions.key_step: Occupancy patterns with arrangements; over-count trap; no option matches
questions.justification: Occupancy-pattern counting with repeated-box arrangement factors and over-count trap; answer is not among the options.

questions.key_step: Solve a,d then compute variance of six numbers
questions.justification: Two linear equations then a mean-square variance computation with six numbers; routine.

questions.key_step: Complement trick: subset sum 203 iff complement sum 7; enumerate
questions.justification: Key idea is the complement (sum 203 iff complement sums to 7) followed by short enumeration; idea is not one every student has met.

questions.key_step: Factorial equation to n^2-13n+30=0 then exclude n=10
questions.justification: Factorial manipulations to a quadratic, then the excluded root and greatest coefficient; routine chain.

questions.key_step: Row-by-row count on non-standard dice
questions.justification: Direct enumeration on small table; one move.

questions.key_step: Two-case conditional probability
questions.justification: Two-case conditional probability; one move.
